items.note: The host /goal is mirrored read-only by goal(host: true) and goal(board); experimental.idle is not registered, so the host keeps sole ownership of continuation.
The opt-in image_generate tool may replace the Codex imagegen transport once it leaves experimental.
A configurable default image model decides whether our transport keeps its current role.
The plugin imports only @opencode/plugin, so removed @opencode/ai providers cannot break it.
Legacy @opencode/ai entry points are not imported anywhere in this tree.
Provider configure types belong to @opencode/ai; the plugin keeps no such types.
Host scheduled prompts are opt-in; our scheduler only runs database maintenance.
The plugin never creates or manages host schedules.
Host image models offered after Codex sign-in may replace the external imagegen path.
Freeform provider tools may change how our JSON tool schemas travel; verify after adoption.
Snapshot capture is host-side and exposes no plugin surface.
Tool output keeps more context headroom; remeasure our large tool results on 2.2.1.
The host retries throttling instead of reporting context overflow; the 2.2.1 defer path stays.
Credential and cache keys stay out of model variants; our generated config adds none.
Prompt-cache settings remain host configuration, matching our no-cache-policy stance.
Git snapshots handle a split index; our worktree commands do not touch the index.
Console web search stays opt-in and the plugin never enables it.
Code Mode reports parse and await failures better; the tawa execute guard is unchanged.
Desktop /reload must be proven against the plugin reload fingerprint before we rely on it.
Desktop follows each plugin server endpoint; our event stream already uses the resolved URL.
The timeline tolerates malformed tool metadata, reinforcing the JSON-safe metadata fix in E-42.
The plugin calls no generated client methods, so the experimental grouping is irrelevant.
Compaction through the Promise AI client needs @opencode/ai, which the plugin does not import.
The plugin declares no Code Mode extension globals or required services.
Desktop plugin manager is experimental; install follow-ups stay frozen until it settles.
Toasts, dialogs, and tabs could replace text-only notices after a host upgrade.
Host image generation may replace the Codex imagegen transport later.
Decision endpoints are not used; routing stays in the plugin for now.
Keyed instructions survive compaction and skip a model turn; adopt after a 2.2.0 host.
Whole-stream mapping is unchanged; filtering is available if profiling asks for it.
Provider cache settings are host configuration; the plugin keeps no cache policy.
The plugin does not import @opencode/ai directly; the external list is unchanged.
TUI-only peer requirement; this plugin ships no TUI surface.
This tree has no GitHub workflows or action references.
Code Mode can surface MCP tools; tawa now refuses execute by name.
Encode failures carry a reference id; the handoff result gap was located and fixed by sanitizing tool metadata.
The host waits for plugin reloads before steps; the fingerprint skip stays.
Schemas convert once per tool; the placeholder and reload contract is unchanged.
Agent and provider lists wait for plugins, narrowing the empty-catalog window.
The dev lane is the desktop sidecar DB; health reports its lane instead of a keyed-path mismatch.
The host retries throttled requests; transient limits defer to it on 2.2.0 and above.
Shutdown cleanup is bounded at 7.5 seconds under the host 10-second cap.
History starts at the latest completed compaction; recheck our context payload after the upgrade.
Fork and rewind become message-level; plugin state has no message anchor yet.
The host releases tool-call memory; RSS is remeasured after the next restart.
Host cost reporting may make our estimate redundant; compare after the upgrade.
SDK-only memory control; our tool results carry no inline file payloads.
Informational endpoint field; the plugin does not identify the machine.
Streamed text survives a finish reason, closing the truncation window tracked in E-15.
Compaction uses the provider token count; our context hook is unaffected.
Sessions and instruction entries survive a deleted project directory.
The background service state directory stays out of tool shells.
Provider-specific schema fix; no Kimi model is pinned in this tree.
External-directory checks use the project filesystem; the pre-flight URL check stays.
